gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for the Amazfit Balance 2, its top pick in one chat: the5krunner measured 33 hours of full-accuracy GPS recording and gave it an 85% GPS-accuracy score on a hard 10-mile run, against OutdoorGearLab's measured 20 hours of GPS for the vívoactive 6.
standout_why: I compared against the cited OutdoorGearLab best-GPS-watch list, the cited Garmin pages (press releases, golf compare page, vívoactive 5 manual), the uncited Panxis battery page, independentgolfreviews.com and the5krunner's Approach upgrade guide. OutdoorGearLab's list gives only the vívoactive 6's measured 20 h GPS and 118 min charge time. It does not cover the Balance 2, any Approach model or golf. Panxis has no measurements of its own and does not cover the Balance 2 or the vívoactives. The independentgolfreviews and the5krunner guide pages give only Garmin ratings for the S12, S44 and S50. Garmin's pages give claims, not tests. None of these pages has a named measurement for the Balance 2, a measured heart-rate accuracy figure for any candidate, or a measured yardage-accuracy figure. Wired (cited) would not load.
decides: This confirms the shortlist rather than changing it. Measured GPS time on the Balance 2 (about 33 h) is about 1.65× the vívoactive 6's (20 h), so both easily cover several rounds on one charge. The vívoactive 6 is the only candidate with a published wrist-heart-rate accuracy figure: a 1.0 BPM median difference from a Polar armband. That favors it for fitness-first buyers. The Balance 2's only golf-distance figure ('within 2–3 yards of a rangefinder', MyGolfSpy) I could read only where Amazfit's blog quotes it. I found no named measurement I could open for the Approach S44 or S12, which also lack wrist heart rate per Garmin.

findings.label: Measured GPS battery life
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab, Matthew Richardson, review dated 2026-05-22: 'We measured 20 hours of GPS battery life in GPS-Only mode' (Garmin claims 21 h). The 20 h figure also appears on the cited OutdoorGearLab best-GPS-watch list.

findings.label: Measured charge time, empty to full
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab spec table, measured. Text: 'Charging from empty to full takes nearly 2 hours.'

findings.label: Measured GPS distance accuracy
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab standard 2-mile course, 2026-05-22. ±0.04 mi over 2 mi is ±2%. Slightly less precise than the dual-frequency watches they tested. Some minor drifting under heavy tree cover.

findings.label: Measured wrist heart-rate accuracy
findings.value: 1.0 BPM median difference from a Polar Verity Sense armband
findings.note: OutdoorGearLab, 2026-05-22. Wrist HR lagged during warm-up. The 1.0 BPM median applies after readings converged at about 15 minutes.

findings.label: Measured full-accuracy GPS recording time
findings.source_title: Amazfit Balance 2 Review: Premium Materials, 14-Day Battery & No Subscription Fees | the5krunner
findings.note: the5krunner (tfk), published 2025-12-05, updated 2026-10-08. Text says 'well over 30 hours'; the pros list says '33-hour sports use'. 33 h ÷ 20 h (OutdoorGearLab, vívoactive 6) ≈ 1.65×. The two sites used different test setups.

findings.label: GPS accuracy score
findings.source_title: Amazfit Balance 2 Review: Premium Materials, 14-Day Battery & No Subscription Fees | the5krunner
findings.note: the5krunner's own scoring on the same route, compared with 30+ other GPS watches. He calls it 'very good by industry standards' but says its routes are 'not market-leading'. This is a running test, not golf yardage.

findings.label: Battery life achieved in daily use
findings.source_title: Amazfit Balance 2 Review: Premium Materials, 14-Day Battery & No Subscription Fees | the5krunner
findings.note: the5krunner, screen set to wake on wrist raise: 'easily lasts two full weeks (sometimes closer to three)'. Amazfit claims up to 21 days.

findings.label: Golf yardage accuracy vs laser rangefinder
findings.source_title: Elevate your round: golf tech built for the smart player | Amazfit blog
findings.note: MyGolfSpy's words ('Always within 2–3 yards of a rangefinder'), quoted on Amazfit's own blog (2025-11-03). The MyGolfSpy original (https://mygolfspy.com/we-tried-it/i-finally-found-a-watch-to-rival-my-1000-garmin/) returned 403, so I read only the maker's reprint. Treat it as unverified until the original is opened.

findings.value: about 5 days with 1–1.5 h of GPS a day
findings.source_title: Garmin Vivoactive 5 GPS Watch Review | CleverHiker
findings.note: CleverHiker, Miles Knotek, updated 2026-05-18: 'hard to make this watch last more than five days with daily GPS recording of 1-1.5 hours and regular smartwatch use.' Garmin claims up to 11 days in smartwatch mode.
